transcript:
Meeting header: 2025-12-04 15:00 PST - 57 min. Attendees: Maya (Redwood AE), Ethan (Redwood SE), Jordan (Redwood SE), Dr. Lena Hart (Astoria CTO), Marcus Lee (Infra), Priya Suresh (Compliance), Oliver (ML lead). Recording quality: medium.

Summary: Discovery focused on on-prem, fully air-gapped deployment for regulated biologics R&D workflows. Key constraints: no egress from subnet, HSM requirement for keys, offline patching process, limited rack power (6kW per rack), preference for certified OS (RHEL 8), and strict audit / retention needs. Customer wants pilot to prove latency and reproducibility with their models and to validate offline update process.

Topics: introductions; compliance expectations (FDA/GxP, NIST mention); hardware constraints and preferred vendors; software packaging and airgap update flow; networking and key management; pilot success criteria and timeline; next steps.

00:00 Speaker 1 (Maya): Hi everyone, thanks for joining. Quick intros from our side - I'm Maya, AE at Redwood Inference -- sorry Redwood Inference, and with me is Ethan, our SE, and Jordan who focuses on private deployments.
00:27 Dr. Lena Hart: Hi, Lena Hart, CTO at Astoria Biologics. We're evaluating options for running large language models on sensitive R&D data, need air-gapped on-prem.
00:40 Marcus Lee: Marcus, infra. We run colo racks and want minimal changes, limited power per rack, and we have a strict change control window.
00:52 Ethan Zhao: Great, thanks. A couple clarifying q's up front: when you say air-gapped, do you mean fully no-egress from the inference cluster to internet? Any offline update channel?
01:06 Priya Suresh: Correct: no egress. Updates happen via signed bundles on physical media, through a jump host that is carefully controlled. We also have an HSM for key material.
01:20 Jordan Kim: Ok noted. When you say HSM, are you using an external HSM appliance (networked) or an on-prem USB HSM token model?
01:28 Priya Suresh: We use an internal nCipher HSM that sits on a separate management VLAN. We'll want KMS integration or the ability to wrap keys for local HSM import.
01:40 Oliver Grund: From ML side - our models are custom Llama-variant quantized 4-bit, but we could run float16 on GPUs if needed. Latency expectation is 150-300ms tail for single-token for inference in a conversational assistant, and throughput during batch scoring is lower priority.
02:05 Ethan Zhao: Ok that helps. For the quantized model, we typically have two options in private: run Redwood runtime with optimized kernels + quant path, or run a containerized engine. For air-gapped we provide signed tarballs of the runtime and model artifacts that can be installed offline.
02:23 Dr. Lena Hart: How do you do offline updates? We cannot have automatic pulls.
02:29 Jordan Kim: We prepare release artifacts — signed manifests and a checksum — the customer transfers them via controlled media; then the install script verifies signature and performs update. We can integrate with your HSM for signature validation or provide a verification key you keep in the HSM.
02:48 Marcus Lee: Power question: our racks are limited to about 6kW per rack. Do you have size/power guidance for GPU requirements? We prefer NVIDIA A2/A10 class or AMD MI300 if supported.
03:03 Ethan Zhao: We can support A10 and Ampere variants; MI300 support is still experimental in our hosted offering but we can bring conversation offline. For power we typically estimate 300-400W per GPU plus overhead — so plan accordingly; we will provide a sizing worksheet.
03:22 Dr. Lena Hart: Does Redwood require any outbound telemetry? We need to ensure no credentials or data leaves environment.
03:30 Maya Patel: For Private/VPC we have an option to disable outbound telemetry and you can opt into sending aggregated metrics via customer-controlled collectors. We also have an air-gap mode that disables cloud callbacks.
03:44 Priya Suresh: On compliance: do you have SOC2 and can we see any GxP-relevant artifacts? We also track data retention and audit logs strictly.
03:55 Maya Patel: Yes, we'll share SOC2 summary and our on-prem security checklist. For audit logs we can emit local logs and structured traces to your syslog/ELK; we don't need to ship logs to Redwood cloud.
04:12 Oliver Grund: On the runtime, what about KV cache and checkpointing? We need to persist session state for longer runs but cannot export anything offsite.
04:22 Ethan Zhao: We support local persistent KV cache and you can configure retention and rotation locally. Checkpoints are stored in local volumes; we can integrate with your storage backend.
04:34 Speaker 6 (Marcus?): Quick question: do we get access to the same Console UI or is that hosted?
04:41 Jordan Kim: For fully air-gapped, the console is a customer-hosted control plane. We provide a private console image that runs in your management network. For partial VPC options you can use Redwood-hosted console with private peering.
04:57 Dr. Lena Hart: We are leaning to fully air-gapped and self-hosted console. We want RBAC mapped to our SAML IdP.
05:06 Maya Patel: We support SAML/SOAR integration; we'll need a SAML endpoint and metadata from you. We also support AD/LDAP sync.
05:18 Priya Suresh: One blocker is software patching windows. We have quarterly change control windows. How fast are security patches applied?
05:28 Ethan Zhao: We recommend an offline patch cadence that aligns with your windows; we provide signed security patches that you can test in staging and then apply during the window. For critical CVEs we can ship a hotfix tarball with instructions and rollback scripts.
05:43 Oliver Grund: On models — do we need to recompile kernels for our quantized weights? What's your support for custom ops?
05:52 Jordan Kim: We have a build pipeline that can include custom kernels; for many quantized Llama forks we use our quant path without recompiling. If you have custom ops we can work with your team to include them in the runtime build as part of the pilot.
06:10 Dr. Lena Hart: Who owns support after install? We want clear SLA and handoff.
06:17 Maya Patel: For Private deployments we offer enterprise support packages. There's an onboarding engagement with Redwood SEs during pilot, then ongoing support with response times tied to your support tier. We can also provide an on-prem concierge during the first 90 days.
06:30 Marcus Lee: A couple of infra specifics: we run RHEL 8, virtualization on KVM, and our management VLAN is isolated. Do you require Kubernetes?
06:40 Ethan Zhao: Our private runtime can run containerized on Kubernetes or as a set of systemd services. For smaller footprints we can do non-k8s deployments. We will send deployment options.
06:52 Priya Suresh: Audit trail: we need immutable logs for at least 7 years for certain artifacts. Can you confirm log rotation and archival options?
07:00 Jordan Kim: We can write audit logs to an append-only store, integrate with your WORM storage, or export to local archive in encrypted tarballs. We'll map to your retention policy in design.
07:16 Oliver Grund: Pilot scope — we'd like a proof with 1) model compatibility test (our quant models), 2) offline update test (signed bundle cycle), and 3) latency profiling under typical request mix. Timeline: Q1 2026 pilot. Is that feasible?
07:35 Maya Patel: Yes, that's feasible. Typical pilot timeline is 6-8 weeks: onboarding, infra prep, run tests, and knowledge transfer. We can compress if needed.
07:45 Dr. Lena Hart: Cost model? We want to compare dedicated reserved capacity vs private self-hosted maintenance.
07:53 Maya Patel: For Private it's a platform license plus optional managed packages. For Dedicated we have reserved GPU pools and Redwood runs the infra; for your use-case where data can't leave, Private is the match. We'll send high-level numbers and a detailed commercial template after this call.
08:08 Marcus Lee: Back to hardware: do you provide any validated hardware SKUs? We'd prefer a short list we can source from our colos.
08:17 Ethan Zhao: Yes, we'll provide validated reference hardware SKUs and power profiles. We'll include both NVIDIA A10G and Ampere options; we'll flag MI300 as experimental and require extra validation.
08:28 Priya Suresh: Encryption at rest and in transit — how do keys get provisioned?
08:35 Jordan Kim: Keys can be provisioned via your HSM. We support KMIP and other HSM integrations. For air-gapped installs, we can provide key wrapping and import instructions.
08:46 Dr. Lena Hart: Any regulatory references you have for GxP?
08:51 Maya Patel: We don't claim GxP certification but provide artifacts that map controls to GxP practices and can support audit evidence. We'll share a mapping doc.
09:00 Oliver Grund: Another technical: GPU sharing and multi-tenant — we'll want strong process isolation between teams and between dev and prod.
09:10 Ethan Zhao: We support tenant isolation through namespaces and process isolation at runtime; for strict separation we recommend dedicated nodes per team.
09:22 Marcus Lee: Do you have any special requirements for network ACLs?
09:27 Jordan Kim: Outbound blocked by default; we need access to your internal package repository for installs or you can place artifacts on the jump host. We'll provide details for firewall rules.
09:38 Dr. Lena Hart: Ok great. Let's recap next steps.
09:42 Maya Patel: Recap from Redwood: we'll send SOC2 excerpts and on-prem security checklist; Ethan will send sizing worksheet; Jordan will prepare offline update walkthrough and signed bundle example; we'll also propose pilot plan and dates.
09:54 Priya Suresh: From Astoria: we'll share power/rack specs, SAML metadata, and change control calendar.
10:03 Maya Patel: Perfect. Any final questions?
10:07 Marcus Lee: No, thanks. We'll look for the docs.
10:10 Dr. Lena Hart: Thanks everyone.
10:12 Meeting ended.

Notes on transcription: occasional mis-heard product names (Redwood Inference in the beginning), speaker label placeholders, occasional filler words and overlap. The transcript includes action items and next steps above.
